transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-17
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Sable Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Sable CTO), Sofia Ruiz (Sable ML Engineer)

---
Summary: High-level discovery focused on integration surface for adding Redwood inference. Customer evaluating hosted for fast time-to-value vs dedicated/private for compliance and predictable latency.

[00:00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm avery from redwood, i'll kick us off — quick intros?
[00:00:12] Maya: hi i'm maya, head of platform at sable, we run a microservices infra on aws, mostly k8s, and we're looking at adding LLM features in our customer support and search flows.
[00:00:25] Liam: liam here, cto, interested in operational cost and latency; we have some regulatory customers that may require data residency.
[00:00:34] Sofia: sofia, ml eng, i'll own the integration with our embeddings/search pipeline.
[00:00:40] Diego: diego, solutions engineer at redwood, i'll cover technical integration, langchain/llamaindex examples, and observability hooks.

[00:01:05] Avery: goal for today is to understand your integration constraints — SDKs, gateway, rate limits, observability — and recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private. feel free to interrupt, we'll go deep where needed.

[00:02:10] Maya: quick context — prod infra in us-west-2, customer data lives in our s3, indexed in elasticsearch currently. we want a hybrid approach: hosted for experimentation but dedicated/private for heavy flows if needed.
[00:02:30] Liam: timeline — POC in 2–3 weeks, pilot in april, but legal/security signoff could push private deployment later.
[00:02:45] Diego: good, that lines up. question on SDKs: are you planning to use our REST api directly or via langchain/llamaindex wrappers?
[00:02:58] Sofia: we'd prefer LangChain for orchestration since we have existing chains, and LlamaIndex for structured retrieval. do you have official connectors?
[00:03:12] Diego: yes we have first-party SDKs in python/js and maintained LangChain/LLamaIndex connectors — sometimes the auto-generated names get a little off in transcripts but code examples are in the integration guide. link: https://redwood.example/docs/integration
[00:03:36] Maya: great; on auth we use a token-based gateway that adds headers and does tenant routing. any caveats with proxies?
[00:03:48] Diego: common pattern — customers put Redwood behind an internal gateway or proxy. we support forwarding of headers, and you can configure token passthrough or a service account. for VPC/private deployments we can integrate with your internal NAT/egress rules. note: if you mutate headers our SDKs expect x-redwood-... but we can be flexible.
[00:04:15] Liam: rate limits — what's throttling like? we have bursts and need predictable tail latency for sync chat flows.
[00:04:26] Diego: hosted tier has tenant rate limits and quota controls; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with throughput SLOs, and Private is fully customer-managed so you control quotas. We expose per-route limits and token-level throttling, and can surface metrics so you can auto-scale upstream.
[00:04:50] Maya: does hosted expose token-level cost and latency per request? we need that for billing back to product teams.
[00:05:02] Diego: yes — Redwood Console has token-level cost, latency breakdown, and per-model dashboards. we also provide tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry) and a metrics endpoint you can pull into prometheus.
[00:05:18] Sofia: retention — hosted stores logs for 90 days by default; for compliance we may need shorter retention or no retention. does dedicated/private change that?
[00:05:29] Avery: dedicated includes options for longer retention or custom retention policies; private you control logs entirely. we can pin down retention in the SLA.
[00:05:40] Liam: security — do you support SAML SSO for the console, and KMS integrations?
[00:05:47] Diego: SSO via SAML/OKTA is supported, RBAC in console, and KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments. we also provide audit logs.

[00:06:20] Maya: back to integration: our gateway rewrites auth headers and terminates TLS. can we use the redwood python SDK inside our services behind the gateway?
[00:06:33] Diego: yes, that's a common pattern. the SDK supports custom transport wrappers so your gateway can inject tracing headers. one caveat: if you do path-based routing and rewrite the URL, ensure the host header is preserved. otherwise the request signing fails.
[00:06:56] Sofia: any sample notebooks for LangChain + LlamaIndex? we saw a community one but would prefer redwood maintained examples.
[00:07:05] Diego: i'll share notebooks — examples include embeddings + vector DB retrieval with LlamaIndex, and multi-step chains with LangChain using Redwood streaming. i'll attach them to the follow-up (Diego -> share by 03/18).

[00:08:22] Maya: curious on quantization/latency tradeoffs. we may run larger models for summarization but lower-cost models for embeddings. how do you recommend?
[00:08:34] Avery: we do model recommendations based on workload. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles. Dedicated supports GPU types optimized for int8 paths which reduce cost with small latency hit; Hosted has curated model profiles.

[00:09:10] Liam: network egress — if we go hosted, does data leave our VPC? what about encrypted uploads?
[00:09:20] Diego: hosted obviously routes through our public endpoints — you can encrypt payloads at rest and in transit; for regulated customers we recommend Dedicated with private peering or Private in-VPC deployment so data never leaves your network.

[00:10:02] Sofia: we use vectordb on prem for vectors — any issues using LlamaIndex to talk to both local vectordb and redwood embeddings?
[00:10:14] Diego: that's normal — you can call Redwood embeddings API to create vectors, store locally, and LlamaIndex can combine local retrieval with remote embeddings. watch out for tokenization differences across models; we document recommended tokenizers in the integration guide.

[00:11:00] Maya: do you support function/tool calling and structured responses for our ticketing system ingestion?
[00:11:10] Diego: yes — streaming + function calling works over the SDKs; we can set strict output schemas and validators. it's good for structured extraction into tickets.

[00:12:20] [00:12:20] Liam: pricing — ballpark hosted costs vs dedicated commit?
[00:12:27] Avery: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token and embedding pricing; Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity with discounts at commit levels. i'll send a pricing sheet after call.

[00:13:05] Maya: any gotchas with client-side rate limiting if we proxy through apigee?
[00:13:16] Diego: proxies are fine; ensure you preserve request ids and tracing headers. also, if your proxy does client-side retry, coordinate backoff to avoid thundering herd into our rate limiting. we can provide a recommended backoff/retry policy.

[00:14:30] Sofia: instrumentation: we'd like spans that correlate request IDs to user sessions, is that possible?
[00:14:40] Diego: yes — we accept custom traceparent headers and will surface span IDs in logs. we support OpenTelemetry so you can correlate. we'll include example setup for prometheus/grafana dashboards.

[00:15:20] Maya: for the pilot, we want a small set of routes: embeddings for search (qps ~ 30), chat completion for support assistant (qps ~ 12, bursty). can hosted handle that?
[00:15:33] Diego: hosted can handle those volumes initially; Dedicated gives you more predictable tail latency. for bursts you can enable autoscale or burst capacity on Dedicated.

[00:16:10] Liam: SLA question — what's the uptime and latency SLO for Dedicated?
[00:16:18] Avery: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime 99.9% and target p99 latency tiers depending on GPU profile; we'll share exact numbers in the SLA packet.

[00:17:00] Sofia: do you support pinning model versions for reproducibility?
[00:17:06] Diego: yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollouts/canary deploys in the console with automatic fallback policies.

[00:18:12] Maya: are there any obvious integration blockers we should be aware of?
[00:18:20] Diego: nothing blocking — main items: gateway header rewrites, proxy retry behavior, and data residency needs. we can provide sample proxies and a troubleshooting checklist.

[00:19:05] Liam: curious about cost allocation — do you surface per-team or per-route cost so we can charge product teams?
[00:19:15] Avery: yes, Console supports per-route and per-token cost breakdown and tagging to tie back to teams.

[00:20:30] [00:20:30] Maya: legal/security: we need SOC2 and ISO docs, and a data processing addendum.
[00:20:38] Avery: we have SOC2 + ISO certs; i'll send the security packet (link: https://redwood.example/security) and DPA template.

[00:21:10] Sofia: any benchmark we can run quickly? like an embedding latency bench with 512 tokens?
[00:21:20] Diego: we can provide a lightweight benchmark harness and a quick script to run 100 requests; or we can run a bench from our side on a dedicated trial instance.

[00:22:05] Maya: what about developer experience — how long to get an account and start sending requests?
[00:22:12] Avery: hosted is immediate — API key in minutes; Dedicated requires provisioning but we can do a fast path pilot with reserved nodes. Private has more lead time.

[00:23:40] Liam: can you speak to fallback policies if a model is rate limited or overloaded?
[00:23:50] Diego: yes — our routing supports fallback to compatible model variants and automated retries with exponential backoff. you can define per-route policies.

[00:24:55] Maya: demo request — can we get a short demo of SDK usage with LangChain?
[00:25:02] Avery: sure we can follow up with a hands-on demo; diego can run through sample code.

[00:26:20] [Diego shares quick code snippet verbally]
[00:26:20] Diego: "from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
from langchain.chains import LLMChain
# example pseudocode - call embedding and chain"
(there's some background noise, and a few words got cut)

[00:27:10] Sofia: perfect, we'll try the sample and report back.

[00:28:00] Maya: one more thing — do you have any guidance for batching embeddings to save cost?
[00:28:08] Diego: yes we recommend batching 16–64 per request depending on payload size; Redwood Optimize can give suggestions based on your traffic shape.

[00:29:44] Liam: internal stakeholders — legal, infra, product — will expect a one-pager comparing hosted/dedicated/private. can you provide that?
[00:29:55] Avery: yes, i'll produce a one-pager and include decision criteria.

[00:31:10] Maya: ok let's talk about pilot acceptance criteria — accuracy of retrieval (mrr@10), latency p95 < 500ms for search, and cost per query under $0.05. are those reasonable?
[00:31:25] Diego: those are reasonable targets; we'll help instrument evals and set up quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.

[00:32:40] Sofia: any special notes for LlamaIndex connectors? we use a custom index layer.
[00:32:50] Diego: LlamaIndex connectors usually talk to your vector store; they can call our embeddings API. the biggest friction is auth and rate limit handling — add retry logic and local batching. we'll supply connector examples.

[00:34:05] Maya: let's align on dates: diego shares notebooks by 03/18, avery sends pricing and one-pager by 03/19, and we aim to spin up a hosted pilot account by 03/29.

[00:34:20] Liam: legal review timeline — likely 2–3 weeks after we get the DPA and security packet.

[00:35:00] Diego: notes on observability — we'll send an OpenTelemetry config and example Grafana dashboards. you can ingest our metrics endpoint into prometheus; we also support direct log export to cloudwatch.

[00:36:30] [small cross-talk about calendar scheduling]

[00:37:00] Maya: thanks, this is helpful. any final questions?
[00:37:05] Sofia: none from me.
[00:37:10] Liam: no.
[00:37:15] Avery: ok quick recap — we'll send pricing, security packet, LangChain/LlamaIndex notebooks, and benchmark harness. diego to schedule technical deep dive for VPC/private.

[00:38:00] Maya: sounds good. thanks team.
[00:38:05] Diego: thanks all — i'll follow up with links.

[00:39:00] [call ends — participants drop off over next minute]
